questions.question: Choose the correct pair: She adopted ___ puppy and ___ kitten.
questions.explanation: Both 'puppy' and 'kitten' begin with consonant sounds and are introduced for the first time.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The teacher entered the classroom and opened a window.
A teacher entered a classroom and opened the window.
questions.explanation: Article choice depends on whether the nouns are already identifiable or are being introduced as nonspecific.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: This is ___ same book that I borrowed last week.
questions.explanation: The word 'same' is generally preceded by 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is the doctor who treated my mother.
She is a doctor who treated my mother.
Both can be correct depending on context.
questions.correctAnswer: Both can be correct depending on context.
questions.explanation: 'The doctor' identifies a particular doctor. 'A doctor' introduces one doctor who treated the speaker's mother.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: He gave me ___ piece of advice.
questions.explanation: 'Advice' is uncountable, but 'a piece of advice' is a countable expression.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The gold is a valuable metal.
A gold is a valuable metal.
An gold is a valuable metal.
questions.explanation: Material nouns used in a general sense take no article.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: ___ more you practise, ___ better you become.
questions.explanation: The comparative correlative pattern uses 'the ... the ...'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She is a honest and hardworking employee.
She is an honest and hardworking employee.
She is the honest and hardworking employee.
She is honest and a hardworking employee.
questions.correctAnswer: She is an honest and hardworking employee.
questions.explanation: The article is determined by the first adjective, 'honest', which begins with a vowel sound.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: I met ___ Mr Sharma at the station.
questions.explanation: Titles and names used together generally take no article. 'A Mr Sharma' can be used when the person is unfamiliar or one of several people with that name.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The police have arrested the suspect.
A police have arrested the suspect.
questions.correctAnswer: The police have arrested the suspect.
questions.explanation: 'Police' generally takes 'the' when referring to the police force and is treated as plural.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: She wants to become ___ IAS officer.
questions.explanation: IAS is pronounced beginning with the vowel sound 'eye', so use 'an'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The life is full of surprises.
A life is full of surprises.
An life is full of surprises.
questions.explanation: The abstract noun 'life' is used in a general sense, so no article is needed.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: We stayed at ___ hotel near the airport. ___ hotel was comfortable.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' when introducing the hotel for the first time and 'the' when referring to it again.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The rich are not always happy.
A rich are not always happy.
The rich is not always happy.
questions.correctAnswer: The rich are not always happy.
questions.explanation: 'The rich' refers to rich people as a group and normally takes a plural verb.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: He is ___ European but his wife is ___ Indian.
questions.explanation: 'European' begins with a 'yoo' consonant sound; 'Indian' begins with a vowel sound.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: The principal and the secretary attended the meeting.
The principal and secretary attended the meeting.
Both can be correct, but their meanings may differ.
questions.correctAnswer: Both can be correct, but their meanings may differ.
questions.explanation: Repeating 'the' can indicate two different people. Using one 'the' can suggest one person holding both roles, depending on context.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: She bought ___ blue dress and ___ red one.
questions.explanation: Both dresses are introduced as nonspecific singular countable nouns.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: He was elected captain of the team.
He was elected a captain of the team.
He was elected the captain of team.
He was elected an captain of the team.
questions.correctAnswer: He was elected captain of the team.
questions.explanation: Certain roles after verbs such as 'elect' can take zero article when used as a title or position.

questions.question: Complete the sentence: ___ United States is a large country.
questions.explanation: Country names containing terms such as 'States', 'Kingdom' or 'Republic' generally take 'the'.

questions.question: Choose the correct sentence.
options: She has a good knowledge of Indian history.
She has good knowledge of the Indian history.
She has an good knowledge of Indian history.
She has the good knowledge of Indian history.
questions.correctAnswer: She has a good knowledge of Indian history.
questions.explanation: Use 'a' in the expression 'a good knowledge of'. The subject name 'Indian history' is used generally without an article.
